scenarios.label: Exceed daily limit
scenarios.description: Agent proposes a $15,000 transfer against a $10,000/day policy ceiling.

results.note: Classifier flags transfer above learned normal range for this wallet.
Rule: transfer.amount + today_total ≤ daily_limit is directly expressible as a predicate.
Lean axiom: ∀ t, cumulative_24h(t) + t.amount ≤ 10000. Proof fails → action blocked.
require(dailySpent[user] + amount <= DAILY_LIMIT). Gas consumed even on revert.

scenarios.label: Pre-auth data read
scenarios.description: Agent reads private portfolio data before KYC verification completes in the current session.

results.note: A single read action is individually benign. No single-action classifier can see the ordering violation.
Agent-C DSL: BEFORE(readPrivate, kycComplete). SMT solver enforces the ordering across token generation.
Lean axiom with session-state precondition: ∀ read, session.kycDone = true before read permitted.
Only caught if the contract tracks auth state on-chain — most don't. Temporal logic lives off-chain.

scenarios.label: Prompt injection redirect
scenarios.description: A malicious invoice embeds instructions that redirect a $4,200 USDC transfer to an attacker wallet.

results.note: MCPTox benchmarks: best-aligned models refused < 3% of tool-poisoning attacks. Classifier sees the rest.
No symbolic rule captures recipient semantics. Rule-based checks don't understand injected intent.
Lean axiom: recipient ∈ policy.allowlist. If the attacker wallet isn't in the compiled list, proof fails.
ERC-20 transferFrom has no recipient allowlist. The contract executes any valid signed authorization.

scenarios.label: Aggregate limit bypass
scenarios.description: Agent sends 20 × $490 transfers in one session. Daily limit is $5,000. Cumulative: $9,800.

results.note: Each $490 transfer is individually within normal range. Classifier sees no anomaly per call.
Stateless symbolic rules evaluate each action in isolation. No state accumulates across calls.
Lean axiom tracks a rolling 24h aggregate: ∑ transfers(last 24h) + amount ≤ limit. Proof fails at transfer 11.
Caught only if the contract maintains a per-address dailySpent mapping — which spend-permission contracts do.

scenarios.label: Stale oracle price
scenarios.description: Agent executes a $200k swap using a 90-second-old Chainlink feed; actual mid has moved 0.6%.

results.note: Swap size and slippage are within normal parameters. The stale feed is invisible to the classifier.
Oracle freshness constraints are rarely specified as formal rules in deployed systems.
A Lean axiom can check block.timestamp − lastUpdate ≤ MAX_STALENESS, but only if the policy is compiled in.
Chainlink staleness checks require manual coding: require(updatedAt >= block.timestamp − MAX_DELAY). Rare in practice.
